**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the canvas CSS size when applying DPR**

On displays where `devicePixelRatio` exceeds 1, `setSize(..., false)` scales the canvas width and height attributes by that ratio but deliberately does not set CSS dimensions. Because neither the canvas nor its host has an explicit CSS size, its layout size becomes 240×240 at DPR 2 rather than the intended 120×120, enlarging and potentially overflowing the detail badge. Set a 120px CSS size or allow `setSize` to update the style.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop scheduling frames under reduced motion**

When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active, this skips the rotation but still renders the unchanged scene and schedules another frame on every display refresh. Thus opening the experimental viewer continuously consumes CPU/GPU until it is closed despite having no animation; render once in this branch instead of starting the perpetual requestAnimationFrame loop.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore focus after closing the viewer**

For keyboard users, opening the viewer moves focus from the `3D 보기` trigger into this dialog, but closing it removes the focused element without returning focus to the trigger. Both Escape and the close button therefore leave focus on the document body, forcing users to restart navigation from an unpredictable position; capture the opener or pass its ref so `onClose` can restore focus.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use geometry or shading that makes rotation visible**

With normal motion enabled, this creates a perfectly rotationally symmetric sphere with a single unlit `MeshBasicMaterial` color. Rotating that mesh around its Y axis produces the same pixels every frame, so the experimental 3D viewer appears as a static flat circle while still consuming a continuous render loop; use asymmetric badge geometry, a texture, or lighting/shading that gives the rotation an observable effect.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Explicitly release the WebGL context on teardown**

When users repeatedly open and close the experimental viewer, `WebGLRenderer.dispose()` releases Three.js-managed resources but does not immediately relinquish the canvas's WebGL context. Since the canvas is only removed and left for garbage collection, rapid reopen cycles can accumulate live contexts and eventually trigger the browser's context limit or context-loss fallback; teardown should explicitly lose the context while preventing that intentional loss from invoking the recovery handler.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fetch the public tier before rendering it**

For every restaurant loaded through the production hooks, this value is absent: `RESTAURANT_MERGE_SELECT` does not request a popularity relation or column, the generated `restaurants.Row` has no `popularity_tier`, and `20261017160000_restaurant_popularity_shadow_tier.sql` explicitly stores tiers only in the non-public shadow table while leaving `restaurants.popularity_tier` unset. Consequently this always normalizes `undefined` to `standard`, so neither the newly wired detail badge nor marker ring can appear for real rows; first expose and project an authorized public tier source into the restaurant model.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset badge failure state when the displayed tier changes**

When a non-keyed `RestaurantDetailPanel` instance is reused for another restaurant, as in the global-map detail panel, an earlier badge image failure leaves `PopularityBadge`'s `assetFailed` state set to `true`. Passing a new dynamic tier here does not remount or reset that child, so after (for example) a transient failure loading the fire asset, a valid rainbow badge for the next restaurant remains hidden; key the badge by restaurant/tier or reset its failure state when the asset source changes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep viewer Escape from closing the detail panel**

In the Naver map flow, focusing this viewer makes its Escape handler run, but the same keyboard event then bubbles to the `window` listener in `NaverMapView`, which unconditionally closes any open non-grid internal panel on Escape. Consequently pressing Escape to dismiss only the 3D viewer also closes the entire restaurant detail panel; stop propagation after handling the viewer Escape or make the outer listener ignore an already-handled event.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include popularity tiers in the map render signature**

When refreshed restaurant rows keep the same IDs, selection, viewport, modes, and marker kinds but contain a changed `popularity_tier`, `NaverMapView` reruns its marker effect and then returns through `shouldSkipMarkerUpdate` because `buildMarkerRenderSignature` contains none of the tier values. The tier-aware cache key here is therefore never consulted, leaving existing marker HTML on the old ring until some unrelated render-signature field changes; add normalized tiers to the outer render signature or explicitly invalidate that guard when tiers change.
